typical_symptoms: Upward cupping or puckering of young leaves
Silvering or bronzing appearance on the underside of leaves
Presence of tiny slender yellow to dark-colored insects along leaf veins
Ragged, torn, or crinkled leaf blades as leaves expand
Stunted growth of seedlings and damaged terminal buds
visual_characteristics: Minute elongated spindle-shaped nymphs and adults visible on leaf surfaces
Silvery or shiny feeding streaks along primary and secondary leaf veins
Tiny black specks of fecal matter (frass) scattered near feeding sites
lesion_characteristics: Rough, scabby scarring without a distinct chlorotic halo
Tiny necrotic flecks scattered along feeding zones
Variable size ranging from microscopic pinpricks to confluent scarred patches
color_characteristics: Insects: translucent pale yellow, amber, to dark brown
Leaf damage: silvery-white to metallic sheen initially, turning bronzed, yellowed, and eventually brown/necrotic along damaged margins
spatial_patterns: Concentrated along main leaf veins and lower leaf surfaces
Irregular scattered feeding trails across tender new growth
distinguishing_features: Direct visual detection of tiny, slender, crawling yellow/brown thrips insects on the leaf surface
Upward cupping of young leaves paired with silvery feeding scars and black frass dots
Damage primarily concentrated on tender young foliage and leaf veins
